paragraphs.text: Green-blue ( or GU ), also called Simic , is an enemy color pair. Their core conflict is nature ( green ) vs. nurture ( blue ). Green and blue have significant mechanical overlap; they share the evergreen keywords flash , hexproof , vigilance , and ward for mana . Green-blue tends toward creature-focused decks, although it lacks the mechanical identity of some other color pairs. The two colors are mutual allies of white ( ).

Green and blue's core conflict is nature vs. nurture . Green believes that everyone's role in the world is predetermined by their genetics (nature), while blue believes that anyone can become anything (nurture). Green accepts the natural world and its own role within that world, while blue seeks to modify and perfect both itself and the world around it.

The two colors share an affinity for information: green seeks wisdom in the past, while blue seeks knowledge to shape the future. Together, they are the most scientific color pair. Green-blue wants to speed along the process of evolution : to study the natural world, then use its findings to improve the world. Because it's so focused on the big picture, it tends to downplay individual concerns; green's acceptance of the world and blue's emotional distance can lend green-blue a stark lack of empathy.
Green-blue heroes include Zimone Wola and Tamiyo while villains include Momir Vig and Oko .

Green and blue share significant mechanical overlap—more than any color pair except green-white and black-red. However, they are thematically disconnected, which can make designs difficult. Green is focused on creatures and tends to operate at sorcery speed , while blue is focused on noncreature spells.

As a deck archetype, green-blue tends to be focused on growing and modifying its creatures. Its path to victory is not set in stone. Blue-green draft archetypes are the most varied of any color pair, often featuring a named set mechanic, because it struggles the most in Limited.
The following mechanics are shared by green and blue.
Winged Coatl - combines the Evergreen mechanics common to green - deathtouch and blue - flash , flying onto one creature efficiently
Yavimaya's Embrace - combines blue's "stealing" creatures from opponents with green's creature boosting "pump" effect and trample
